summary: 5 solder steps for 8 parts: resistors, transistor, electrolytic capacitor, switch, connector; danger at C1, J2.

steps.action: Solder the resistors R1 (1 kΩ), R2 (10 kΩ), R3 (100 kΩ), R4 (100 kΩ) flat on the board.

hints.text: Low parts early, so the board lies flat while you solder (rule of thumb).
Point the colour bands the same way; that makes checking the values easier (rule of thumb).

steps.action: Solder the transistor Q1 (2N2222A); match each pin to its pad.

hints.text: Pinout from the datasheet, do not guess: in the same TO-92 case the onsemi PN2222 is pin 1-2-3 = E-B-C, the onsemi P2N2222A is C-B-E.
Keep each joint short and let the part cool before the next joint (rule of thumb).

steps.action: Solder the electrolytic capacitor C1 (10 µF 16 V); the stripe on the sleeve marks minus.

hints.text: Polarised: reverse voltage can open the pressure relief vent (Nichicon). The stripe on the sleeve marks the negative lead (Rubycon). Confirm the polarity before soldering.
The iron must not touch the capacitor body (Nichicon).
Do not tilt, lay down or twist the body once it is soldered (Nichicon).
Press the switch flat onto the board while you solder the first pin (rule of thumb).
J2: laser. Never look into the beam and never aim it at anyone (FDA). Keep the laser unplugged while you solder (rule of thumb).
Solder one pin, check the alignment, then solder the rest (rule of thumb).

warnings.message: C1: Polarised: reverse voltage can open the pressure relief vent (Nichicon). The stripe on the sleeve marks the negative lead (Rubycon). Confirm the polarity before soldering.
J2: laser. Never look into the beam and never aim it at anyone (FDA). Keep the laser unplugged while you solder (rule of thumb).
Orientation matters for Q1 (transistor); check each mark before soldering.

assumptions.value: mechanical parts last; low before tall; robust before heat-sensitive

assumptions.reason: no iron temperature without the datasheets of your solder and parts; use their values

assumptions.value: C1: above its rail, with margin
assumptions.reason: not in the BOM; over-voltage can vent it (Nichicon); the margin is a rule of thumb (datasheet)

sources.title: Practice rule, not a standard
sources.note: Shown for engineering judgement only; check the datasheet of your parts.
